name: Grade 6 T3: 3D Modeling and Project Sharing
description: 3D modeling tools, shapes, movement, resizing, rotating, duplicating, grouping, prototypes, presentations, and feedback.

words.definition: Having three dimensions: length, width, and height.
words.example: A 3D model can be viewed from different sides.

words.definition: A digital or physical version of an object or idea.
words.example: The student built a 3D model of a desk organizer.

words.definition: A basic form used to build a model.
words.example: The model used cubes, cylinders, and spheres.

words.definition: A 3D shape with six equal square faces.
words.example: The student used a cube for the base of the model.

words.definition: A 3D shape with two circular ends and one curved side.
words.example: A cylinder made the pencil holder part.

words.definition: A round 3D shape like a ball.
words.example: The sphere was used as a decorative part.

words.definition: To change where an object is placed.
words.example: The student moved the shape to the center of the workplane.

words.definition: To make an object larger or smaller.
words.example: The cylinder was resized to become taller.

words.definition: To turn an object around an axis.
words.example: The student rotated the shape to make it face the correct direction.

words.definition: To make a copy of an object.
words.example: The student duplicated a shape to create two matching sides.

words.definition: To combine objects so they work as one object.
words.example: The shapes were grouped after they were aligned.

words.definition: To place objects neatly in relation to each other.
words.example: The student aligned the shapes before grouping them.

words.definition: The flat digital surface where 3D objects are placed and edited.
words.example: The model sat on the workplane.

words.definition: A plan for how something should look or work.
words.example: The design included a sketch and labeled shapes.

words.definition: A quick drawing that plans an idea.
words.example: The sketch showed where each shape would go.

words.definition: An early version of a design used for testing and improvement.
words.example: The 3D model was a prototype of a useful desk item.

words.definition: The reason something is made or used.
words.example: The model purpose was to hold pencils.

words.definition: A change that makes something better.
words.example: The planned improvement made the model stronger.

words.definition: A picture of what is shown on a screen.
words.example: The student submitted a screenshot of the 3D model.

words.definition: To show and explain work to an audience.
words.example: Each student presented a chart, spreadsheet, or 3D model.

words.definition: Helpful comments about what works and what can improve.
words.example: A partner gave feedback about making the model easier to understand.

words.definition: A short explanation of what was made, improved, or learned.
words.example: The reflection described one change made after testing.

words.definition: A finished piece of work made during a project.
words.example: The chart was one project artifact the student could present.

words.definition: A guide that explains how work will be checked or graded.
words.example: The rubric listed the required parts of the model.
